article_title: Curricular uptake of virtual gaming simulation in nursing education.
citation: Verkuyl M., Lapum J.L., St-Amant O., Hughes M., Romaniuk D. (2021). Curricular uptake of virtual gaming simulation in nursing education. Nurse Education in Practice. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nepr.2021.102967
title: Virtual gaming simulation (VGS): high-fidelity 2D immersive branching-scenario games for nursing clinical decision-making
description: VGS integrate gaming theory with computerized simulations re-enacting clinical scenarios. The article's games are described as "a high fidelity, 2D immersive simulation using videos of simulated patients (played by actors)" in which users make clinical decisions. A branching scenario approach presents film clips of nurse-client scenarios with options; incorrect choices show consequences and feedback before redirection, and users receive a summary report and can replay. Games cover pediatrics, mental health, maternal health, and emergency, are freely accessible, take up to an hour to play, and have been played over 600,000 times across 25 counties.
requirements: Alignment of VGS learning outcomes with course learning outcomes, standards of practice, and entry-to-practice competencies
Faculty and technological support available so glitches do not overshadow the experience
constraints: High quality VGS are expensive to produce, though unlimited reuse mitigates some costs
Open access with no log in means the team does not know players' disciplines, year of nursing, or demographics
examples: The games are freely accessible at de.ryerson.ca/games/nursing/hospital and have been integrated into curricula at the authors' institutions, internationally, and for continuing competence
